title: Unique Crunchy Peruvian Cashew Chupe De Camarones
description: A winey, crisp, and adventurous Peruvian dish featuring cashews, cooked in a clay pot, and suitable for Jain-friendly diets. This form of chupe de camarones is a twist on the traditional Peruvian shrimp stew.
instructions: Heat the clay pot over medium heat and add the chopped onion to saute until translucent.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the sliced aji amarillo peppers and cook for 2 minutes, until they start to soften.
Add the white wine and bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping the bottom of the pot to release any browned bits.
Add the vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, and peeled shrimp, and stir to combine.
Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture simmer for 10 minutes, or until the shrimp are pink and fully cooked.
Stir in the unsalted cashews and cook for an additional 2 minutes, until they are lightly toasted and fragrant.
Season the chupe de camarones with salt and pepper to taste, then stir in the chopped fresh cilantro.
Serve the chupe de camarones hot, garnished with additional chopped cilantro if desired.
